display.purpose: Hero H1, section H2s, standalone big numbers (process step numbers, metrics).

body.purpose: Hero paragraph and section descriptions; reading copy only.

label.purpose: Every functional string, in two sub-styles: Metadata (uppercase, tracking-[0.16em] — eyebrows, tags, durations, captions) and Action (sentence case, untracked — nav links, button text, footer links).

shadows.name: hero-lift
shadows.purpose: Reserved for the hero browser-mockup illustration only — the page's one hero object. No other surface uses a shadow.

shadows.name: instrument-bezel
shadows.purpose: Scoped to gauge/dial faces only (gauge.tsx GAUGE_BEZEL_SHADOW). A recessed instrument rim, not a raised/projected shadow — the Flat-by-Default Rule's one other exception.

motion.name: cursor-blink
motion.purpose: Blinking cursor in the hero mockup's address bar; respects prefers-reduced-motion (duration forced to 0.01ms).

motion.name: color-transition
motion.purpose: Default hover/focus transition for links, buttons, and card borders.

motion.name: gauge-sweep
motion.value: transform: rotate() transition 900ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), triggered once by IntersectionObserver at 40% visibility
motion.purpose: Needle sweeps from rest to its real value when a MetricsBar gauge scrolls into view, overshooting slightly before settling — see instrument-settle.

motion.name: dial-sweep
motion.value: @keyframes dial-sweep, 2.4s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), 88%-to-100% overshoot step (96deg -> 90deg), triggered once by IntersectionObserver
motion.purpose: Process dial's needle sweeps through all 4 detents once, overshooting past the fourth detent before settling on it (Delivery), when the dial scrolls into view.

motion.name: instrument-settle
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) on the Gauge needle; an explicit overshoot keyframe step on the Process Dial
motion.purpose: Deliberate exception to 'no bounce/elastic easing' — a calibrated physical instrument has spring and mass, so its needle overshoots its real value by a small amount before settling, rather than gliding to a flat stop like a UI tween. One restrained overshoot, not an oscillating spring; suppressed narrowly in the detector config with this reasoning on record.

motion.name: switch-flip-press
motion.value: transform: scale(0.9) translateX(-4px) on :active, 150ms, reverts on release
motion.purpose: Switch Glyph actuator dot nudges toward 'off' on press then springs back on release — the tactile confirmation stays satisfying on the hundredth click, not just the first.

motion.name: hero-rise
motion.value: @keyframes hero-rise, 600ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), staggered ~80ms per element, fill-mode both
motion.purpose: The page's one focal entrance: eyebrow → headline → paragraph → CTA row → browser-mockup arrive as one authored beat on hero mount. Pure CSS, no script dependency. Never reused elsewhere.

motion.name: switch-pulse
motion.purpose: One-time power-on pulse on the hero's primary Switch Glyph actuator, timed to land just after the hero-rise sequence finishes. Hero only — nav/CTA-section switches stay static.

motion.name: drawer-in
motion.value: @keyframes drawer-in, 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), fill-mode both, replayed on every mount
motion.purpose: Mobile nav drawer rises and fades in each time it opens; closing stays an instant unmount.

motion.name: reveal-stagger
motion.value: transition: opacity/transform 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), ~60ms per-sibling delay, hidden state applied post-mount via JS (reveal.tsx)
motion.purpose: Sibling-stagger scroll reveal, reserved for genuine lists (Portfolio cards, Process steps) only — never a blanket per-section fade-up. Defaults to fully visible if script fails.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.value: transform: scale(0.97) on :active, part of the bare `transition` utility (~150ms)
motion.purpose: Primary switch buttons (hero/nav/CTA-section WhatsApp+Orçamento) compress slightly on press for tactile confirmation before navigation.

motion.name: card-hover-zoom
motion.value: transform: scale(1.04) on the card image, scale(1.25) on the lit dot, 300ms, clipped by the card's own rounded corners
motion.purpose: Portfolio card hover — reinforces the card as a selectable channel, reusing the Switch Glyph's dot-scale idiom instead of a new hover device.

motion.name: instrument-tilt
motion.value: transform: rotateX()/rotateY(), capped +/-7deg, rAF-throttled pointermove, 100ms linear while tracking / 600ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) on release, perspective(900px) on the stage (hero-mockup-stage.tsx)
motion.purpose: Overdrive hero moment: the mockup tilts as one rigid plane toward the pointer, like a physical panel viewed off-axis. Desktop/fine-pointer only; the pointermove listener is never attached under prefers-reduced-motion or on coarse/no-hover pointers.

motion.name: power-trace
motion.value: @keyframes power-trace, 3s total cycle (~1.4s active draw/hold/fade, ~1.6s paused) cubic-bezier(0.65,0,0.35,1), 950ms initial delay, infinite iteration, SVG stroke-dashoffset 1->0 then opacity 1->0 then hold (power-trace-frame.tsx)
motion.purpose: Overdrive hero moment: a Signal Blue line traces the mockup's frame, holds, fades, pauses, then draws again — the frame reads as its normal Hairline border between passes. First pass timed to start as the hero-rise entrance settles; the loop is paused via IntersectionObserver/visibilitychange whenever the mockup isn't visible.

motion.name: dark-veil
motion.value: WebGL shader canvas (ogl), requestAnimationFrame loop, dialed-in preset (hueShift 20, speed 1, resolutionScale 1.25, noise/scanline/warp off), opacity-[0.3] — dark-veil-background.tsx wrapping vendored DarkVeil.jsx/.css (react-bits). resolutionScale > 1 forced safe via a scoped `[&_canvas]:w-full! [&_canvas]:h-full!` override (ogl's Renderer.setSize otherwise writes an inline CSS box sized off the same scaled value, overflowing the viewport-filling container).
motion.purpose: The system's one deliberately colorful, expressive layer, fixed behind the entire page (negative z-index, painted before normal content), not just the hero. Unmounted whenever the tab is hidden (visibilitychange) and skipped entirely under prefers-reduced-motion. Replaces the earlier hero-only Flow Field, which is unused but left in the repo.

scrollbar.value: thin; thumb Hairline (#23232a) on Ink (#0a0a0a) track, 2px Ink inset border, Console Gray (#68686c) on hover — scrollbar-color for Firefox, ::-webkit-scrollbar* for Chrome/Safari/Edge
scrollbar.purpose: Themes the one browser-default surface craft-floor calls out by name — scrolling reads as part of the built instrument, not a leftover default.

components.description: The system's only button variant — Signal Blue outline on transparent background, JetBrains Mono label. Used for every primary action (WhatsApp CTA, nav budget link).

components.name: Ghost Link
components.description: Lower-emphasis text action (nav links, secondary hero CTA). No border, no fill — just an opacity/color shift on hover. narrative.overview:
lander.co reads like a dark IDE or terminal at work past midnight: near-black canvas, a single raised panel tone for cards, hairline borders standing in for structure, and JetBrains Mono carrying every functional label the way a CLI carries status text. Space Grotesk handles the few moments that need to speak — headlines, big numbers — with a tight, confident tracking. Signal Blue, the one accent, behaves like an active cursor or a syntax highlight: it marks the word that matters, traces a button's edge, blinks once in the hero mockup's address bar, and otherwise stays out of the way. Nothing is filled that doesn't need to be; the system earns its technical credibility by looking like something a developer actually built, not something a template generated.

Depth is almost entirely denied. Two background tones (ink for the page, a barely-lighter surface for panels) plus 1px hairline borders do the work that shadows would do elsewhere — the hero's browser-mockup illustration and the instrument dials are the only exceptions. Every other surface stays flat at rest.

Layered onto that base is a page-wide compositional device, "Painel de Controle Industrial": every metric, the process pipeline, and every primary action reads as a labeled instrument or switch on one control-panel fascia, rather than as a stat, a list, or a link. This is a composition choice, not a new identity — the palette, type, and every rule still govern it; it adds instrument shapes (circular gauges, a rotary dial, a switch glyph) and one narrow depth exception, never a new material, color, or font.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black canvas with a single raised-surface tone for panels — no gradient backgrounds.
Signal Blue used as a marker (outline, dot, single word, blinking cursor, gauge needle), never as a fill.
JetBrains Mono for every functional/label string; Space Grotesk for display type; Inter for reading copy.
Flat by default — hairline borders and background-tone shifts carry structure instead of shadows, except the instrument faces' bezel.
A single reusable identity motif — the browser-window brand mark with an arrow "landing" inside it — appears at multiple scales (nav, footer, favicon, hero illustration).
Metrics, process, and primary actions read as instruments and switches on a shared control-panel fascia.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: There is no separate gray scale for secondary/tertiary text. Every text hierarchy step below full-strength Paper White is expressed as an opacity of paper — /90, /70, /60, /50, /40, /25. Never introduce a new gray hex; step the opacity instead.

rules.name: The No-Fill Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue never becomes a background fill outside of a 10% hover tint. Primary actions are always outline buttons — a solid blue button would break the system's restraint. Exception: ::selection is a solid Signal Blue highlight, since text selection is transient and user-triggered, not part of the static composition.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Function Rule
rules.body: If a string is a label, action, or piece of metadata it is set in JetBrains Mono, usually uppercase with wide tracking. If it's a sentence meant to be read, it's Inter. Display type is reserved for headlines and standalone numbers.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: No card, button, or panel casts a shadow at rest or on hover. If something needs to feel elevated, that's a signal it should be the page's hero object, not a routine surface. Amendment (approved for the instrument-panel composition): a circular gauge or rotary dial face may carry the Instrument Bezel — a recessed rim, never a raised/projected shadow. No other component earns this exception.

dos: Do treat text hierarchy as opacity steps on Paper White (/90 → /25), not as a separate gray palette.
Do set every label, nav item, button, tag, and metadata string in JetBrains Mono, uppercase with wide tracking at small sizes.
Do keep Signal Blue rare and marker-like — one accent word, an outline, a dot, never a fill beyond a 10% hover tint.
Do keep the interface flat; use background-tone and border changes, not shadows, for hover/state feedback.
Do scale the brand mark rather than redrawing its geometry.

Do collapse pending/unfinished items into one compact indicator instead of one placeholder card per item, and omit a section entirely when it has zero real content rather than shipping a permanent placeholder in its place.
Do keep the Instrument Bezel scoped to gauge/dial faces only, keep every dial aria-hidden, and document how a gauge's needle fraction was derived alongside the real, sourced value it illustrates.

Do keep motion to one focal entrance (the hero power-on) plus a small set of named, purposeful supporting moments (sibling-stagger reveal for genuine lists, press feedback, hover feedback, drawer continuity) — never a blanket per-section scroll-fade.
Do default every scroll-triggered reveal to fully visible in the server-rendered markup, applying the hidden pre-state only after mount via JS, so a blocked or failed script never hides content.

Do style every custom error/empty state (e.g. not-found.tsx) with the same Nav/Footer/Container shell as the rest of the site, leading with the plain-language problem and a real recovery action — never leave a route on an unstyled framework default.

Do keep the Overdrive tilt/power-trace pair confined to the hero mockup — the one place on the page that has earned an extraordinary moment. Every other card/section stays at the restrained Motion vocabulary above.

Do lock any third-party/vendored decorative background or effect to this system's exact Signal Blue (hue 227, no range/jitter) rather than that vendor's own default palette or hue spread — one accent color across the whole page, including borrowed components.
donts: Don't introduce a filled/solid Signal Blue button — every button in this system is outline-only.
Don't add drop shadows to routine cards, buttons, or panels; the hero browser-mockup shadow and the Instrument Bezel are the system's only two depth exceptions, both named above.
Don't set body copy or reading paragraphs in JetBrains Mono, or labels/metadata in Inter — the font choice is functional, not aesthetic preference.
Don't fabricate a new neutral gray hex for a text-hierarchy step; step Paper White's opacity instead.
Don't let a decorative dial's caption or label duplicate text a screen reader already gets from real content nearby — hide the decorative copy instead.
Don't replay the hero's power-on sequence or switch-pulse anywhere else on the page — it stays the one authored entrance moment.
Don't animate layout-driving properties (width, height, top, left, margin) for scroll reveals or hover states — transform and opacity only.
Don't reach for bounce/elastic easing anywhere outside the named Instrument Settle motion — that one exception is grounded in the panel's own mechanism, not a general license for playful easing.
Don't joke, trivialize, or invent content on an error state — lead with the plain-language problem and a real recovery action.
